# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

## Overview

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design in small sections (200-300 words), checking after each section whether it looks right so far.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**
- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**
- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**
- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Break it into sections of 200-300 words
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

## After the Design

**Documentation:**
- Write the validated design to `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Implementation (if continuing):**
- Ask: "Ready to set up for implementation?"
- Use superpowers:using-git-worktrees to create isolated workspace
- Use superpowers:writing-plans to create detailed implementation plan

## Key Principles

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design in sections, validate each
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

content.text:
Locked in:

> **Spine:** Evolution of the human — senses → mind → hands · **Voice:** cryptic & mysterious · **Style:** hybrid ASCII + blueprint · **This session:** directions + copy, no code yet.

Everything below shares one story skeleton. The three *directions* differ only in how that skeleton is dressed — so you're choosing a **design language**, not a different site. Let me give you the skeleton first, then three ways to wear it.

---

## The scroll spine (shared by all three)

The page is one long vertical descent. Each beat earns the next. The throughline: *being human is not a fixed thing — and we build the extensions.*

```
00  HERO          the company + the thesis: "the next human sense"
01  MANIFESTO     what we believe · stretch the borders · who we are
02  THE FRAME     "the human is being extended in three directions"
                  → 01 senses   02 mind   03 hands
03  SENSES        smart glasses   — the eyes of the system   [upcoming]
04  MIND          GAIA            — the mind of the system   [LIVE]
05  HANDS         robotics        — the hands of the system  [upcoming]
06  CONVERGENCE   "not three products. a different kind of person."
07  CLOSING       the crazy ones · talk to us · social
```

The existing braille "march-of-progress" art becomes the literal hinge at **02 → The Frame** (evolution made visible), and the GAIA section is the only one allowed to "light up" as live — everything else reads as *in fabrication*, which is what makes the page feel mysterious instead of salesy.

Sample of the **shared cryptic voice** (this tone is constant across all three directions):

> *Humanity has always reached past its own edges.*
> *We build the reach.*
>
> *Glasses for the senses. An intelligence for the mind. Machines for the hands.*
> *Three extensions of one idea — that being human is not a finished thing.*

---

Now the three design languages. Each shows a **hero** and a **product card** so you can feel it.

## ◾ Direction A — TERMINAL / OBSERVATORY

*The site boots up like you're logging into the company's nervous system.* A persistent status line, typewriter reveals, blinking cursor, faint scanline. Most overtly "hacker."

- **Type:** Doto for labels, a clean mono (Geist/JetBrains) for body · **Color:** black + phosphor-white + one dim accent only on `LIVE`
- **Motion:** lines *type themselves in*; sections glitch-fade on entry; cursor pulse
- **Feel:** alive, systemic, a little uncanny

```
  experience://boot
  > initializing humanity ............... ok
  > loading senses ...................... ok
  > loading mind ........................ ok
  > loading hands ................... pending

  WE ARE BUILDING THE
  NEXT HUMAN SENSE_▌
  [ scroll to continue ] ▼
```
```
  ── 02 / mind ───────────────────── [ LIVE ]
  GAIA
  > an intelligence that holds your life
    so your mind can wander further.
  $ status: online   $ learning: you
  → heygaia.io
```

## ◾ Direction B — BLUEPRINT / FIELD MANUAL  *(my recommendation)*

*The site reads like a declassified hardware document.* Dimension lines, schematic wireframes, dotted leader lines, `FIG. 0X` headers, spec tables. This is the purest expression of "wireframe + ASCII + sci-fi + mysterious," and it makes the *upcoming* products feel like real classified hardware.

- **Type:** Doto for headers/specs, mono for annotations · **Color:** black + white + `zinc-800` blueprint lines + dashed borders (you already use these)
- **Motion:** schematic lines *draw themselves*; leader dots fill left-to-right; spec rows stagger in
- **Feel:** precise, engineered, secret-project

```
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ THE EXPERIENCE COMPANY    DOC 00 · REV A│
  ├───────────────────────────────────────┤
  │   THE NEXT HUMAN SENSE                  │
  │   ▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔                  │
  │   subject ........ homo sapiens         │
  │   objective ...... extend the edges     │
  │   status ......... in fabrication       │
  └───────────────────────────────────────┘
```
```
  FIG. 01 — SENSES                    [UPCOMING]
  ╭──────────────────────────────────────────╮
  │     ◉━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━◉     ← 41 g         │
  │    ╱   smart glasses   ╲                  │
  │   └─ 38mm ─┘    └── display ──┘           │
  ╰──────────────────────────────────────────╯
  the eyes of the system .................. 01/03
```

## ◾ Direction C — MONOLITH / VOID

*The most minimal and mysterious.* One idea per screen, oceans of black, ASCII used only as rare monumental moments. The story unfolds like stanzas. Closest to "premium," furthest from "techy."

- **Type:** Doto, large, sparse · **Color:** pure grayscale, no accent · **Motion:** slow fades, drifting dot-field parallax, generous hold
- **Feel:** cinematic, reverent, gallery-like

```



            the experience company


        WE ARE BUILDING
        THE NEXT HUMAN SENSE


              ·   ·   ·
                 ▼
```
```


        02

        gaia.
        the mind of the system.

        it already exists. it already works.
        →
```

---

**My take:** **B (Blueprint) as the backbone** — it's the strongest fit for everything you asked for and gives the *upcoming* products gravity — **borrowing C's negative-space restraint for the hero and the 02→Frame transition**, and optionally a single A-style status line in the footer as a living heartbeat. That blend is dark, precise, mysterious, and unmistakably "stretching what's possible."

Which way pulls you — **A, B, C, or a blend** (e.g. "B but more void")? Once you point, I'll write the **complete section-by-section copy deck** (every headline, sub, spec line, and the convergence + closing) plus a layout/motion spec for the winning language.

message.content: i donbn't like the copy you've written doesn't sound like something steve jobs would say. i like direction b. but like i want it to be subtle. not too many headings. just images and text normally. and i guess border style layout of the entire webpage could be used too (like some companies like vercel or cursor do) with the grid layout.  and i don't like the eyes of the system and mind of the system shit it sounds weird.

content.text:
Got it — that's clear feedback. Three corrections I'm taking:

1. **Copy** → plainer, warmer, more certain. Jobs didn't do cryptic. He did *simple truths said with conviction* — concrete, human, a little understated. No "reach past our edges," no "X of the system." Cutting all of it.
2. **Layout** → Direction B's *feeling*, but expressed as a **bordered grid scaffold** (the Vercel/Cursor hairline frame), subtle. Fewer headings. Just images and normal text sitting in the grid.
3. **Drop** the "eyes/mind/mind of the system" taglines entirely.

Let me re-show both. Copy first, since that was the miss.

---

## The copy (Jobs voice — plain, certain, human)

**00 · Hero** — wordmark, then one line. Three to react to:

> **A.** We build technology that makes people more capable.
> **B.** Technology should give you your life back. We're building the technology that does.
> **C.** We're building a better experience for being human.

*(I lean A — it's the most Jobs: plain subject, plain verb, no adjectives hiding the idea.)*

**01 · Who we are** — a short paragraph, no heading needed:

> We're a small team of hackers, engineers, and designers. We build the things we wish existed.
> We think the best technology gives you more and asks for less — more time, more attention, more room to be human — and then gets out of the way. Most technology today does the opposite. We're building the other kind.

**02 · The work** — three products, each just a small label + an image + two lines. No big headers.

> `smart glasses — in development`
> A screen you never have to look down at. Glasses that hand you what you need the moment you need it, then disappear.

> `gaia — live today`
> A personal assistant that actually knows you. It keeps track of your life so you don't have to, and gives the day back to you. → heygaia.io

> `household robotics — in research`
> The work that fills a home and empties your hours. We're building machines to take it off your hands.

**03 · Why it's one thing, not three**

> Glasses, an assistant, and machines for the home sound like three different bets. They're not. They're one idea: take the friction out of being alive, so people have room to do what only people can do.

**04 · Close** — keep the Jobs quote you already have (it fits now), then:

> If you want to help build this, we'd love to meet you.  ·  email · github · x

---

## The layout (bordered grid — Vercel / Cursor)

The wireframe *becomes the page itself*. A constrained centered column (~720px) held between two faint vertical hairlines that run the full height. Sections divided by horizontal hairlines, `+` marks at the intersections. Everything subtle — `zinc-800` lines on pure black. Images and text just live in the cells, normally.

```
 +─────────────────────────────────────────────────+
 |                                                   |
 |   the experience company                          |
 |                                                   |
 |   We build technology that makes                  |
 |   people more capable.                            |
 |                                                   |
 +──────────────────────────+────────────────────────+
 |                          |                         |
 |   We're a small team of  |   [ faint wireframe ]   |
 |   hackers, engineers...   |                        |
 |                          |                         |
 +─────────────────────────────────────────────────+
 |  smart glasses                    in development   |
 |                                                    |
 |        ◉───────────────────────────◉               |
 |       ╱     [ glasses wireframe ]    ╲              |
 |                                                    |
 |  A screen you never have to look down at.          |
 +─────────────────────────────────────────────────+
 |  gaia                                  live today  |
 |   ...                                  → heygaia   |
 +─────────────────────────────────────────────────+

Good instincts — both of those *were* slop tells, and I'll own that: "they're not, they're one idea," "take the friction out of being alive," and the "see with you, think with you, work beside you" triple are exactly the cadences that read as machine-written. Let me fix all three things.

## 1. How we keep this from feeling like AI slop

The whole difference is **specifics + restraint**. The rules, short version:

**Copy**
- **Concrete beats abstract, always.** "Shows the name of the person you just shook hands with" beats "powerful, seamless AR." If a line would survive on *any* company's site, it's slop — cut it.
- **Kill the tells:** no "it's not X, it's Y," no "we don't build products, we build…," no tidy triples, no "imagine a world," no *empower / unlock / elevate / seamless / harness*. Go easy on em-dashes (my bad).
- **Admit the hard parts.** Slop is always certain and frictionless. "This is the hardest thing we'll build" is something only a real team writes.
- **Vary the rhythm.** Short. Then one longer sentence that earns it. Not everything parallel, not everything polished.
- **Say the thing a committee wouldn't.** An actual opinion is the most un-fakeable signal.

**Images** — line-art/blueprint was a *good* anti-slop choice (no plastic skin, no melted geometry). Still: generate 10 and keep 1, no embedded gibberish text, check the hands, and where you can use the *real* thing (actual GAIA UI, a real photo) over a generated stand-in.

**Design** — no gradient-on-dark, no glassmorphism, no floating 3D blobs, no brain-with-circuits icon. The restraint *is* the brand. A little quiet and a little asymmetric reads as human; perfectly glossy and centered reads as generated.

(Now written into the doc as its own section.)

## 2. Fixing the "one thing, not three" section

Dropping the heading and the cleverness. Two plainer options — I recommend the first because it answers a real question and has a point of view:

> **A (recommended).** People ask why a software company is building glasses and robots. We don't really think of ourselves as a software company. We're trying to make people more capable, and that problem doesn't stop at the screen — some of it lives on your face, some of it lives in your house.

> **B (plainer still).** Three products, one reason: the work of running your life shouldn't fall on you. Software that knows you, hardware that goes with you, machines that act for you.

content.text:
This is exactly the raw material I needed — and there's a lot of it. My job here is editorial: the fastest way *back* to slop would be to dump all 20 features on the page. A mysterious teaser earns its power by showing the few most striking, concrete things and trusting the reader. So I curated hard.

Here's the distilled glasses section. It uses a **spec-sheet treatment** — which is perfect, because the blueprint design language *is* a spec sheet. Lead copy, then a dotted-leader list that lets us show real substance while staying scannable and on-brand:

**Lead**
> GAIA, on your face. A display only you can see, a camera that sees what you see, and an assistant you just talk to. It paints your directions onto the road ahead, picks up the call you don't want to take, and remembers the things you'd have forgotten by dinner. You run it with your voice, your eyes, and your hands — no controller, no phone in your palm.
>
> Most smart glasses are bricks you'd never wear in public. These are meant to be light, cheap, and good-looking enough that you forget they're smart at all.

**Spec list** (renders as the blueprint dotted-leader list)
```
display ........ visible only to you
voice .......... "hey gaia"
navigation ..... directions painted on the road, live
memory ......... auto-captures what's worth keeping
control ........ voice · eye-tracking · blink · finger gestures
calls .......... gaia can screen and answer them
audio .......... bone conduction, ears stay open
lenses ......... clear → sunglasses, one press
power .......... solar across the whole frame
build .......... light, affordable, and not ugly
```

**What I deliberately left off the page** (kept in your product spec — just not teaser material): pricing/subscription, the SDK + "fix the App Store" platform strategy, eye-biometric login, and phone-pairing mechanics. The platform ambition is too good to fully bury, so I'd hint at it with *one* optional line and nothing more:

> *Underneath, it's a real OS — open for anyone to build on, and ship to in a single click.*

A few editorial notes on why this works as anti-slop: "bricks you'd never wear in public" and "not ugly" are real opinions only you'd say. "Forgotten by dinner" and "directions painted on the road" are concrete images, not adjectives. The spec list earns its length because it's information, not marketing.

Folding this into the doc now.

Good — this is the part that's hard to feel from prose. Let me walk you down the actual page, top to bottom, as wireframes. First the frame, then each section as it scrolls past.

## The frame (constant on every screen)

Everything lives inside a centered **~720px column** held by two faint vertical **rails**. Black gutters fall away on both sides. Horizontal hairlines split the sections; a small `+` sits where a rule meets a rail.

```
   black gutter        ║   ~720px column   ║        black gutter
   (just black)        ║   all content     ║        (just black)
                       ║   lives in here   ║
        the two rails ─╨───────────────────╨─ run the full page height
```

The rails and `+` marks are the *only* "blueprint" chrome. Because they carry the structure, the text and images inside can stay calm.

---

## The scroll, section by section

**00 · HERO** — near full-screen, text only, lots of black.

content.text:
Two good questions — and they're connected, because clean line art is what *makes* animation easy. Let me take them in order.

## 1. Balancing detail vs. clean outlines

The target is: **read the silhouette first, then a few internal lines — and nothing more.** Too sparse looks unfinished; too dense turns into noise and starts looking "AI-busy," which kills the blueprint clarity. A good rule of thumb: **strong outline + ~3–6 internal lines per object**, plus 1–2 blueprint accents (a dimension line, a callout circle). Those accents read as *information*, not decoration, so they add richness without clutter.

The biggest lever isn't adding detail — it's **banning the noise-makers.** Shading, gradients, hatching, and texture are what muddy line art. Say no to them explicitly.

**Prompt modifiers to keep handy:**

*Dial detail DOWN (if it's busy/tangled):*
```
simple, clean, minimal detail, single consistent line weight, no shading, no gradients, no crosshatching, no texture, generous negative space
```
*Dial detail UP (if it's too bare):*
```
add a few internal panel lines and joint details, thin dimension lines with small tick marks, one or two circular callout magnifiers
```

Two more things that matter as much as the prompt:
- **Consistency across the set.** Same line weight, same detail level on every image. One over-detailed image makes the whole page look auto-generated. (Pick one image you like, then describe its density in the others.)
- **The squint test.** Generate, then squint at the thumbnail. If it reads as one clean shape → keep. If it's a bird's nest → "simpler, fewer lines." This is where the "generate 10, keep 1" rule earns its keep.

Keep strokes pure white, thin, even — that not only looks cleaner, it's exactly what animates well, which is the next part.

## 2. Animating them — yes, several ways

Ranked by fit for *this* aesthetic:

**① SVG line-draw — the "blueprint drawing itself" (best fit).** The lines trace themselves on as you scroll into the section. It's the single most on-brand effect for a blueprint site, it's crisp at any size, and it's basically free in bytes. The catch: it needs the art as **vector (SVG)**, not the raster PNG GPT gives you. The path:
> generate clean line art → trace to SVG (Illustrator *Image Trace*, [vectorizer.ai](https://vectorizer.ai), or `potrace`) → animate with `stroke-dashoffset`.

This is *why* Q1 matters — clean, high-contrast, thin-line art traces to clean SVG. Busy art traces to garbage. So keeping them minimal pays off twice.

**② Real-time 3D wireframe (Three.js) — for the GAIA orb.** A wireframe sphere that slowly rotates and breathes looks alive in a way a static image can't, and it's ~20 lines of code. Ideal for the planet; optionally the robot. No image needed at all.

**③ Subtle CSS/JS on the PNGs as-is (zero vector work).** Fade-and-rise on entry (already planned), slow parallax drift, a faint opacity pulse, or a mask "wipe" that reveals the image left-to-right. Low effort, works on the raster files directly. Good baseline for everything.

**④ AI image-to-video (Runway / Kling / Luma / Sora / Pika).** Feed a still in, get a short loop out — the fingers slowly closing in "the touch," the dissolve actually dissolving. Export as a muted looping WebM. *Use sparingly* — it's heavier, harder to keep consistent, and AI video is where the "slop" risk creeps back. Reserve it for **one** cinematic moment at most.

**My recommendation:** SVG line-draw for the blueprint pieces (glasses, robot, the touch, evolution) + a Three.js wireframe for the GAIA orb + the uniform fade-rise on everything. That gives you motion that's crisp, lightweight, and unmistakably "engineered" — and it all honors `prefers-reduced-motion` by just showing the finished art. Skip AI video unless you really want the fingers to touch.

Want me to add this as a section in the design doc (detail-balance modifiers + the animation plan)? And the §03 A/B + commit calls are still open whenever you care to close them.

content.text:
Fair to push me on it. Let me audit my own claims honestly — a couple were solid, one I oversold.

**Holds up:**
- `stroke-dashoffset` line-draw is a real, standard technique. ✓
- It needs **vector**, not the raster PNG GPT gives you. ✓
- Three.js wireframe orb being easy and native. ✓ (and it sidesteps the whole problem below, since it's *born* as wireframe)
- AI image-to-video tools exist. ✓

**What I oversold — the trace-to-draw path:**

The gap: "trace the PNG → animate the stroke" doesn't actually work the way I implied. When you trace line art with potrace / vectorizer / default Illustrator Image Trace, you get **filled shapes** — each drawn line becomes a thin closed blob that's *filled*, not a *stroked path*. `stroke-dashoffset` on a fill does nothing. So you can't just trace-and-draw; that was me hand-waving.

To get a *true* self-drawing line you need **centerline** vector strokes — either centerline tracing (`autotrace --centerline`, or Illustrator's centerline mode, which is finicky and needs cleanup) or honestly just **redrawing it as strokes by hand** in Figma/Illustrator. That's real work, not "basically free." And "free in bytes" was only true for simple SVGs — auto-traced detailed art can be thousands of nodes and genuinely heavy.

**So the corrected, honest plan:**

1. **GAIA orb (and maybe the robot)** → Three.js native wireframe. No tracing, actually easy, looks alive. This is the clean win.
2. **Glasses / touch / evolution PNGs** → a **mask-wipe / `clip-path` reveal** (a moving mask uncovers the finished PNG as you scroll) plus the fade-rise. This *reads* as "drawing in," works directly on raster, and is genuinely low-effort. ~90% of the effect, none of the tracing pain.
3. **True stroke self-drawing** → only worth it for one or two hero pieces you're willing to hand-build as SVG strokes. Don't promise it for all of them.
4. **AI video** → still a sparing one-moment option, same slop caveat.

The detail-balance advice from before (silhouette + 3–6 lines, ban shading/hatching, the squint test, consistency across the set) — that part I'll stand behind; it's just composition judgment, nothing technical to get wrong.

Net: the *idea* (crisp, engineered, scroll-driven motion) is right; my "just trace it" shortcut was wrong. Mask-reveal + Three.js is the real route.

content.text:
Hell yeah — this is where it gets fun. The trick with "cool details" is they have to feel like they belong to the *system*, not decoration bolted on. Everything below extends the blueprint/grid logic you already have. The danger is doing all of them — pick ~5 and it reads crafted; do 12 and it's noise. I've starred the ones I'd actually ship.

## Extending the grid/blueprint theme
- **★ Crosshair cursor** — replace the default arrow with a thin `+` reticle. Single most on-brand thing you can do; the whole site instantly feels like an instrument.
- **★ Corner crop-marks** — little camera-framing ticks `⌐ ¬ ⌐ ¬` pinned to the four corners of the viewport. Frames the whole page like a spec sheet.
- **★ Gutter section indices** — tiny `01 — 05` running down the margin beside each section. Blueprint wayfinding, costs nothing, looks expensive.
- **Dimension annotations** — a faint `├─── 720 ───┤` measurement line over the hero, or `←41g→` ticks on the glasses image. Pure engineering-drawing chrome.
- **Faint graph-paper grid** behind everything at ~3% opacity — the column "sits on" blueprint paper.

## Atmosphere (kills the flat-digital look)
- **★ Film grain + vignette** — a 3–5% noise overlay and a soft edge-darkening. This is the difference between "CSS demo" and "premium." Almost every great dark site does it; you won't consciously notice it, but you'll feel it.

## Interaction personality (no scroll-animation, just hover/state)
- **★ Bracket link hovers** — `email` → `[ email ]` on hover. Terminal-flavored, quietly delightful.
- **Spec-row hover** — the dotted leader fills solid or the value brightens to white. Makes the spec sheet feel interactive.
- **Crosshair focus rings** — keyboard focus draws a reticle, not a browser outline. Accessibility *and* craft.

## The "mysterious" lever
- **★ Redacted specs** — render upcoming/secret details as `████████` or blurred, with a `[ classified ]` tag. You *already* blur upcoming names on the live site — lean all the way in. Robotics especially: half its spec line redacted = intrigue.
- **Console easter egg** — ASCII logo + a hidden line for anyone who opens devtools. Costs nothing, signals craft to exactly the people you want to hire.
- **Custom 404 / `humans.txt`** in the same language.

## Drama through contrast
- **One full-bleed break** — every section respects the 720 column *except* the connection climax (evolution → the touch), which blows past the rails edge-to-edge, then snaps back. Restraint everywhere makes that one moment hit.
- **Version tag** in the footer — `v0.1 · the experience company` in mono. Tiny, but reads as "engineers made this."

---

**My starter pack (the 5 I'd wire in first):** crosshair cursor · corner crop-marks · gutter section indices · film grain + vignette · bracket link hovers. Together they transform the feel without adding a single new word or breaking the restraint. Then redacted specs + the full-bleed break for the mystery/drama.

Want me to **build the starter 5 into the prototype right now** so you can see them live? I can keep each one toggle-able so if any feels like too much, we kill it in one line.

---
import { Font } from "astro:assets";
import "../styles/global.css";
import Footer from "./Footer.astro";
import Navbar from "./Navbar.astro";
import GoogleAnalytics from "../components/GoogleAnalytics.astro";
import { siteConfig } from "../config/site";

interface Props {
  title?: string;
  description?: string;
  image?: string;
  url?: string;
  lang?: string;
  canonical?: string;
}

const {
  title = siteConfig.name,
  description = siteConfig.description,
  image = siteConfig.ogImage,
  url = siteConfig.url,
  lang = siteConfig.lang,
  canonical = url,
} = Astro.props as Props;

const siteName = siteConfig.name;
const fullTitle = title;
const twitterCard = siteConfig.twitterCard;
const ogImage = image.startsWith("http") ? image : `${siteConfig.url}${image}`;
---

<html lang={lang} class="bg-black text-white sm:p-10 p-5">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <title>{fullTitle}</title>
    <meta name="description" content={description} />
    <meta name="keywords" content={siteConfig.keywords.join(", ")} />
    <meta name="author" content={siteConfig.author} />
    <link rel="canonical" href={canonical} />
    <link rel="sitemap" href="/sitemap-index.xml" />
    <link
      rel="sitemap"
      type="application/xml"
      title="Image Sitemap"
      href="/image-sitemap.xml"
    />

    <Font cssVariable="--font-main" preload />

    <!-- Open Graph -->
    <meta property="og:locale" content={lang} />
    <meta property="og:type" content="website" />
    <meta property="og:title" content={fullTitle} />
    <meta property="og:description" content={description} />
    <meta property="og:url" content={canonical} />
    <meta property="og:site_name" content={siteName} />
    <meta property="og:image" content={ogImage} />
    <meta property="og:image:secure_url" content={ogImage} />
    <meta property="og:image:type" content="image/png" />
    <meta property="og:image:width" content="1200" />
    <meta property="og:image:height" content="630" />
    <meta property="og:image:alt" content={fullTitle} />

    <!-- Twitter -->
    <meta name="twitter:card" content={twitterCard} />
    <meta name="twitter:site" content={siteConfig.social.twitter} />
    <meta name="twitter:creator" content={siteConfig.social.twitter} />
    <meta name="twitter:title" content={fullTitle} />
    <meta name="twitter:description" content={description} />
    <meta name="twitter:image" content={ogImage} />
    <meta name="twitter:image:alt" content={fullTitle} />

    <meta name="theme-color" content="#000000" />

    <!-- Favicons -->
    <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico" sizes="32x32" />
    <link rel="icon" href="/logo.svg" type="image/svg+xml" />
    <link rel="apple-touch-icon" sizes="180x180" href="/apple-touch-icon.png" />
    <link rel="icon" type="image/png" sizes="32x32" href="/favicon-32x32.png" />
    <link rel="manifest" href="/site.webmanifest" />

    <!-- Google Analytics -->
    {
      siteConfig.googleAnalyticsId && (
        <GoogleAnalytics id={siteConfig.googleAnalyticsId} />
      )
    }

    <!-- Head slot for page-specific additions -->
    <slot name="head" />
  </head>

  <body class="space-y-4 sm:max-w-2xl mx-auto">
    <Navbar />

    <main id="content" class="space-y-4">
      <slot />
    </main>

    <Footer />
  </body>
</html>

---
import { Font } from "astro:assets";
import "../styles/global.css";
import Footer from "./Footer.astro";
import Navbar from "./Navbar.astro";
import GoogleAnalytics from "../components/GoogleAnalytics.astro";
import { siteConfig } from "../config/site";

interface Props {
  title?: string;
  description?: string;
  image?: string;
  url?: string;
  lang?: string;
  canonical?: string;
}

const {
  title = siteConfig.name,
  description = siteConfig.description,
  image = siteConfig.ogImage,
  url = siteConfig.url,
  lang = siteConfig.lang,
  canonical = url,
} = Astro.props as Props;

const siteName = siteConfig.name;
const fullTitle = title;
const twitterCard = siteConfig.twitterCard;
const ogImage = image.startsWith("http") ? image : `${siteConfig.url}${image}`;
---

<html lang={lang} class="bg-black text-white sm:p-10 p-5">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <title>{fullTitle}</title>
    <meta name="description" content={description} />
    <meta name="keywords" content={siteConfig.keywords.join(", ")} />
    <meta name="author" content={siteConfig.author} />
    <link rel="canonical" href={canonical} />
    <link rel="sitemap" href="/sitemap-index.xml" />
    <link
      rel="sitemap"
      type="application/xml"
      title="Image Sitemap"
      href="/image-sitemap.xml"
    />

    <Font cssVariable="--font-main" preload />

    <!-- Open Graph -->
    <meta property="og:locale" content={lang} />
    <meta property="og:type" content="website" />
    <meta property="og:title" content={fullTitle} />
    <meta property="og:description" content={description} />
    <meta property="og:url" content={canonical} />
    <meta property="og:site_name" content={siteName} />
    <meta property="og:image" content={ogImage} />
    <meta property="og:image:secure_url" content={ogImage} />
    <meta property="og:image:type" content="image/png" />
    <meta property="og:image:width" content="1200" />
    <meta property="og:image:height" content="630" />
    <meta property="og:image:alt" content={fullTitle} />

    <!-- Twitter -->
    <meta name="twitter:card" content={twitterCard} />
    <meta name="twitter:site" content={siteConfig.social.twitter} />
    <meta name="twitter:creator" content={siteConfig.social.twitter} />
    <meta name="twitter:title" content={fullTitle} />
    <meta name="twitter:description" content={description} />
    <meta name="twitter:image" content={ogImage} />
    <meta name="twitter:image:alt" content={fullTitle} />

    <meta name="theme-color" content="#000000" />

    <!-- Favicons -->
    <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico" sizes="32x32" />
    <link rel="icon" href="/logo.svg" type="image/svg+xml" />
    <link rel="apple-touch-icon" sizes="180x180" href="/apple-touch-icon.png" />
    <link rel="icon" type="image/png" sizes="32x32" href="/favicon-32x32.png" />
    <link rel="manifest" href="/site.webmanifest" />

    <!-- Google Analytics -->
    {
      siteConfig.googleAnalyticsId && (
        <GoogleAnalytics id={siteConfig.googleAnalyticsId} />
      )
    }

    <!-- Head slot for page-specific additions -->
    <slot name="head" />
  </head>

  <body class="space-y-4 sm:max-w-2xl mx-auto">
    <Navbar />

    <main id="content" class="space-y-4">
      <slot />
    </main>

    <Footer />
  </body>
</html>

It's built and verified. **Live now at → http://localhost:4321/**

## What I built

The full Astro revamp, structured cleanly:

```
src/
  layouts/      Layout (frame + overlays + console egg), Navbar (top bar), Footer (braille + version)
  components/
    ui/         Section · ImageFrame · Redacted
    sections/   Hero · Manifesto · SmartGlasses · Gaia · Robotics · Connection · Close
  styles/       global.css  ← the whole design system
  pages/        index.astro (composes sections, SEO/JSON-LD preserved) · 404.astro
public/         humans.txt
```

**Every detail you liked is in:**
- ✅ Bordered-grid frame — centered 720px column, rails, `+` crosshairs at every divider
- ✅ Crosshair reticle cursor (custom SVG, falls back to native)
- ✅ Corner crop-marks pinned to the viewport
- ✅ Gutter section indices `00–06` running down the margin
- ✅ Film grain + vignette overlays (subtle, ~3.5%)
- ✅ Bracket link hovers `[ email ]`, spec-row hover, dotted-leader spec list
- ✅ Redacted `████` "classified" field-of-view spec on the glasses
- ✅ Full-bleed climax — the connection section breaks the rails edge-to-edge
- ✅ Version tag + braille sign-off in the footer
- ✅ Console easter egg + custom 404 + `humans.txt`
- ✅ Doto display / JetBrains Mono body, the one green `● live today` accent, reduced-motion respected

**Placeholders:** the 6 images are on-theme dashed blueprint frames with `fig. 0X` captions — swap them via `ImageFrame`'s `src` prop when you generate the art (no markup changes needed).

## A couple of notes
- `pnpm build` fails on a **pnpm policy** (sharp/esbuild build scripts need approval) — *not* our code. I built with `./node_modules/.bin/astro build` to bypass it. To fix permanently, run `pnpm approve-builds` and pick sharp + esbuild.
- `prototype.html` is still in the root — want me to delete it now that the real thing exists?
- Still uncommitted (per your call). Since you're on `master`, when you're ready I'd branch first, then commit.

Open it and tell me what to tune — spacing, the grain intensity, cursor feel, the green accent, type sizes. What's your first read?

input.content:
## What

A full redesign of **experience.heygaia.io** — the umbrella site for The Experience Company (GAIA, smart glasses, household robotics).

It's now a single dark, mysterious, scroll-told story in a **bordered-grid "blueprint" design language**: a constrained, centered column held by hairline rails and `+` crosshairs, Doto display type over a JetBrains Mono body, on a pure-black canvas.

## Sections

`00` hero (three-line thesis) · `01` manifesto · `02` smart glasses (spec sheet) · `03` GAIA (live — the one accent) · `04` household robotics · `05` the connection (full-bleed climax) · `06` close.

Copy is written in a plain, confident, Jobs-ish voice — GAIA's section is verified against the live product + manifesto; robotics leans on the "AI should do the grunt work, not the art" thesis.

## Crafted details

- Crosshair reticle cursor · corner crop-marks · gutter section indices
- Film grain + vignette atmosphere
- Bracket link hovers `[ … ]` · dotted spec-leaders · spec-row hover
- A redacted `████` "classified" spec on the glasses
- Full-bleed connection climax that breaks the rails
- Console easter egg · custom `404` · `humans.txt` · footer version tag
- One green `● live today` accent (GAIA only); everything else monochrome
- `prefers-reduced-motion` respected

## Structure

```
src/components/ui/         Section · ImageFrame · Redacted
src/components/sections/   Hero · Manifesto · SmartGlasses · Gaia · Robotics · Connection · Close
src/styles/global.css      the design system
src/layouts/               Layout (frame + overlays) · Navbar (top bar) · Footer
src/pages/                 index.astro · 404.astro
public/humans.txt
docs/plans/                full design + copy + image prompts
```

All existing JSON-LD / SEO metadata is preserved.

## Notes

- **Images are on-theme blueprint placeholders** (dashed frames with `fig. 0X` captions). Swap them in via `ImageFrame`'s `src` prop — no markup changes needed. Copy-paste GPT image prompts are in `docs/plans`.
- `astro.config.mjs` adds **JetBrains Mono** (`--font-body`) alongside Doto.
- Verified with `astro build` (clean). Note: `pnpm build` needs `pnpm approve-builds` for sharp + esbuild in this environment.

## How to review

`pnpm dev` (or `./node_modules/.bin/astro dev`) → http://localhost:4321/
